title: Coefficient 7/2 at exponent 1: 3.5n - o(n) B2 gates for one fixed uniform family in P

claims.statement: Joint CircuitBreaker theorem under rules.md: the following declaration defines ONE fixed eligible total uniform NP family in the pinned full B2 model at actual input length n. Its full guarantee and its declared projection both hold unconditionally, for all sufficiently large integer lengths with the quantifiers specified by the theorem kinds. Both score source claims assert this ENTIRE declaration, not separate lemmas. For g(n)=c*n^p*(log2 n)^q*(log2 log2 n)^r with the exact parameters in guarantee, liminf over all integer n of C_B2(f_n)/g(n) >= 1. Equivalently, for every epsilon>0 there is N_epsilon such that C_B2(f_n)>=(1-epsilon)*g(n) for every integer n>=N_epsilon. Declaration: {"convention":"uniform-np-full-b2-actual-length-all-lengths-v1","family":"One fixed total family f_N on {0,1}^N, defined for every integer N>=1 by proof.md Section 1. Set k(m) = the least prime > 2*m^(3/5) and N(m) = m + k(m); let m(N) be the largest m with N(m) <= N. Read the input as a prefix q in {0,1}^k with k = k(m(N)), a payload y in {0,1}^m with m = m(N), and an ignored tail. Let Q(Z) = Z^k + sum_{i<k} q_i Z^i. If Q is not irreducible over F_2 the value is 0; otherwise, in F = F_2[Z]/(Q) with polynomial basis 1..Z^(k-1), split the payload into r = ceil(m/k) k-bit blocks (zero-padded last block) giving phi_i(y) in F, put y_i = phi_i(y)^(2^(i+1)-1), let Sym_r^t be the t-th elementary symmetric polynomial with t = ceil(sqrt(r)), and output the constant coefficient of Sym_r^t(y_1,...,y_r). The same deterministic polynomial-time algorithm (prime scan, Rabin irreducibility test, field arithmetic, division-free symmetric-polynomial recurrence) computes every f_N; the language is in P, hence in NP with empty witnesses.","guarantee":{"coefficient":{"denominator":"2","numerator":"7"},"exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"kind":"polynomial_log","log_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"},"loglog_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"}},"projection":{"coefficient":{"denominator":"2","numerator":"7"},"exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"kind":"finite"},"theorem":"For this one fixed total uniform family, at actual input length N and in the full Li-Yang B2 model, C_B2(f_N) >= (7/2)*N - 67*N^(4/5) for every integer N >= 2^10; hence liminf over N of C_B2(f_N)/N >= 7/2, so the declared finite projection (7/2, 1) holds. Proof: fix a valid prefix and the zero tail, restricting to an m(N)-dimensional affine slice on which f_N is the Ben-Sasson-Kopparty affine disperser of dimension floor(6*m^(4/5))+1; the slice circuit computes that disperser, so the gate elimination theorem for affine dispersers (framework.md, Theorem A: every B2 circuit for an affine disperser of dimension d has at least 3.5n-7d gates) gives C_B2(f_N) >= (7/2)*m(N) - 42*m(N)^(4/5) - 7, and m(N) >= N - 7*N^(3/5) - 1 yields the stated remainder. Both directions of NP membership, all integer lengths and an explicit N_epsilon = max(2^10, ceil((67/epsilon)^5)) are established in proof.md.","version":"circuitbreaker-expression-v1"}
